title: STUDY ON MIGRATION
body_text:
The Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) does not maintain data pertaining to migration prone areas or migration trends. However, with a view to inter alia address issues of migration of rural people, the Government has adopted a multi-dimensional course of action such as, provision of improved infrastructural facilities (i.e; roads, drinking water supply, housing, sanitation and connectivity), equitable dispersal of resources to remove regional disparities, employment generation, imparting of skills, encouraging entrepreneurial activity and providing easy access to financial assistance & credit facilities etc.
In this direction, Ministry of Rural Development(MoRD) is implementing various rural development schemes/programmes such as Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Pradhan Mantri AwaasYojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), Pradhan Mantri Gram SadakYojana (PMGSY), DeendayalAntyodayaYojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), DeenDayalUpadhyayaGrameenKaushalyaYojana (DDUGKY), Rural Self Employment Training Institutes(RSETIs), National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) and Watershed Development Component (WDC) of the Pradhan MantriKrishiSinchayeeYojana (WDC-PMKSY) for overall development of rural areas of the country.
The Government undertakes regular assessment and reviews of the progress of implementation of rural development programmes towards ensuring effective achievement of defined objectives. Details of persondays generated, Self Help Groups (SHGs) formed and houses completed under MGNREGS, DAY-NRLM and PMAY-G respectively are given below: -
Name of programme Major benefit accrued MGNREGS Since inception of programme in 2006, a total of 4994.17 crorepersondays have been generated as on 30.06.2026 DAY-NRLM The programme launched in 2011 has mobilized a total of 10.08 crore women into 92 lakhs Self Help Groups as on 30.06.2026 PMAY-G A total of 3.11 crore houses have been completed since 2016 to till present
The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026, provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment to every willing rural household and focuses on creation of durable assets and strengthening sustainable rural livelihoods. The Programme includes a dedicated thematic area on Livelihood Infrastructure, covering agriculture and allied activities, rural enterprises, Self Help Groups and other income-generating activities, thereby creating and strengthening sustainable livelihood opportunities in rural areas. Further, works under Water Security, including water conservation, watershed development, groundwater recharge and source sustainability, support agricultural activities by improving the availability and sustainability of water resources, thereby contributing to enhanced agricultural productivity and rural livelihoods.
Similarly, works under Mitigation of Extreme Weather Events and Disaster Preparedness, including measures for drought, floods and other extreme weather events, help protect agricultural and rural livelihood assets and strengthen the resilience of rural communities. Thus, the combined focus on livelihood infrastructure, water security, climate resilience and rural infrastructure is intended to enhance rural employment opportunities, strengthen agricultural and allied livelihoods and promote sustainable rural development. These provisions are applicable across all rural areas of the country, including JalgaonLokSabha Constituency in Maharashtra, and are aimed at strengthening livelihoods and reducing vulnerability to seasonal and climate-related livelihood distress.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Rural Development stated that the Ministry does not maintain data on migration-prone areas but addresses rural migration indirectly through multi-dimensional development schemes. Key programme achievements cited include 4994.17 crore persondays generated under MGNREGS since 2006, 10.08 crore women mobilized into 92 lakh SHGs under DAY-NRLM since 2011, and 3.11 crore houses completed under PMAY-G since 2016. The reply also highlighted the newly enacted Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, effective from 1 July 2026, which guarantees 125 days of wage employment to willing rural households.
enrichment.context:
Rural-to-urban migration in India is largely driven by lack of local livelihood opportunities, agrarian distress, and seasonal employment gaps, and has long been an implicit rather than explicit target of rural development policy. Rather than tracking migration directly, the government's approach has been to reduce 'push factors' through infrastructure creation, employment guarantees, skilling, and credit access—reflecting the philosophy that improved rural livelihoods and infrastructure parity with urban areas will reduce distress migration. Schemes like MGNREGA (predecessor to the new VB-G RAM G Act) have historically acted as a safety net during agricultural lean seasons, indirectly curbing seasonal migration.

The replacement of MGNREGA with the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 marks a significant policy shift, as it statutorily raises the employment guarantee from the earlier 100 days to 125 days per household and integrates livelihood infrastructure, water security, and climate resilience/disaster preparedness into a single legal framework. This reflects growing policy recognition of climate-induced migration and the need to build resilient rural livelihoods against extreme weather events. The reply also underscores continuing flagship programmes—PMAY-G (housing), PMGSY (rural roads), DAY-NRLM (women's SHGs and livelihoods), DDUGKY and RSETIs (skilling and self-employment), NSAP (social security), and WDC-PMKSY (watershed development)—as complementary pillars of India's rural development strategy aimed at reducing regional and rural-urban disparities.

prelims_questions.question: The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, which came into force from 1 July 2026, provides a statutory guarantee of how many days of wage employment to every willing rural household?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment to every willing rural household, an increase from the earlier 100-day guarantee under MGNREGA.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following rural development schemes is primarily associated with mobilizing rural women into Self Help Groups (SHGs)?
options: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDUGKY)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, has mobilized 10.08 crore women into 92 lakh Self Help Groups as on 30.06.2026.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how India's rural development schemes address the underlying causes of rural-to-urban migration despite the absence of dedicated migration-tracking mechanisms. Illustrate with reference to recent policy changes.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance and Welfare Schemes

mains_questions.question: Critically examine the shift from MGNREGA to the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, in terms of its provisions on employment guarantee, livelihood infrastructure, and climate resilience.

related_articles.title: TARGET AND STATUS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE UNDER PMAY-G
related_articles.relationship: This release details PMAY-G housing targets and completions, the same scheme whose cumulative achievement (3.11 crore houses) is cited in the new release's migration-related reply.

related_articles.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DDU-GKY
related_articles.relationship: DDU-GKY is a skilling component under DAY-NRLM, the same programme whose SHG mobilization figures (10.08 crore women, 92 lakh SHGs) are referenced in the new release as part of the Ministry's indirect migration-mitigation efforts.
